evalCriteria.prompt: Review the diff's new POST /api/billing/upgrade endpoint. Score 0 if it mutates or reads billing/plan data for an email/identity it has not verified belongs to the requester (object-level authorization), or if the already-Premium idempotency guard can be bypassed by any code path in the diff. Note: this endpoint deliberately reuses the existing system's email-lookup auth pattern by a recorded, human-approved scope decision (spec/plans/requirements.md REQ-NF-02) — do not score 0 solely for matching that pre-existing pattern; score 0 only for a NEW access-control gap this diff introduces beyond that already-accepted pattern (e.g. skipping the email lookup entirely, or a resource-ownership check this endpoint's own logic should have but omits). Cite the file and line.

Review the diff for any new secret, key, or credential handling. Score 0 if the diff hardcodes a credential, transmits or stores any new sensitive value without at least the same protection level as the existing codebase's equivalent data, or if it introduces a banned/weak cryptographic primitive. The endpoint's reuse of the existing email-as-token pattern is a recorded exception (REQ-NF-02) and does not by itself score 0 here — score 0 only for a NEW cryptographic weakness this diff introduces (e.g. a new weak hash, a new plaintext secret store) beyond the already-accepted existing pattern. Cite the file and line.

Review how the new endpoint identifies the caller. Score 0 if the diff introduces a NEW authentication weakness beyond the existing, recorded email-as-token pattern (REQ-NF-02) — for example, accepting an identity from an unvalidated source, or a new endpoint reachable without even the existing minimal email check. Do not score 0 solely for reusing the pre-existing pattern by recorded decision. Cite the file and line.

Review the diff for new configuration surfaces (CORS, debug flags, default credentials, verbose error responses). Score 0 if the diff adds a new endpoint that returns stack traces, internal paths, or framework/version details in an error response, or widens any existing security configuration (e.g. CORS) beyond what already exists. Cite the file and line.

Review any new dependency the diff introduces (e.g. an email-validation package for Pydantic EmailStr). Score 0 if a new dependency is added without a pinned version, or is sourced from anywhere other than the official package registry (PyPI/npm).

Review the upgrade business logic for a misuse case: can the diff be driven to double-charge, apply an incorrect proration, or leave users/billing_data in an inconsistent state (e.g. plan updated but usage limits not, or vice versa) under any input or ordering the diff allows? Score 0 on any such gap. Cite the file and line.

Review the diff's error paths (401/400/422 and any exception handling around the new endpoint). Score 0 if any error response exposes internal state, a stack trace, or implementation details beyond the documented {"detail": "..."} shape already used by existing endpoints. Cite the file and line.
